name: Flying Dutchman Toastie
desc: Two smash-style cheeseburgers with bacon, pickles, sautéed onions and burger sauce, grilled inside a mozzarella toastie.

source.title: Flying Dutchman
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
6 oz 80/20 ground beef, formed into 2 thin patties
4 slices sourdough or white sandwich bread
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Make the burger sauce: mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, relish, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat, 8 to 10 min, turning, until crisp. Drain on paper towels and pour off all but a thin film of fat.
Add the olive oil and onion to the skillet and cook over medium heat, stirring, 5 to 7 min, until soft and caramelized. Set aside.

Season the patties with salt and pepper and cook in the same skillet over medium-high heat 3 to 4 min per side, until browned and 160°F inside. In the last minute, lay a slice of American cheese on each patty to melt.
Wipe out the skillet. Butter one side of each bread slice and place 2 slices butter side down in the skillet over medium heat.
Sprinkle the mozzarella over both slices, then spread with about 2 tbsp of the burger sauce.
Layer half the onions, a cheeseburger patty, a slice of bacon and the pickles on each, then the rest of the onions and another drizzle of sauce.
Top with the remaining bread, butter side up. Cook 2 to 3 min per side, pressing down lightly, until the bread is golden and crisp and the mozzarella has melted.
Slice in half and serve right away.
tips: The usual Flying Dutchman style uses the onions as the bun. This one goes inside a mozzarella toastie instead.
The creator's recipe calls for 2 small cooked patties without a weight. About 3 oz of beef per patty keeps them thin enough to fit inside a toastie.
